title: High Fade vs Low Fade: Picking by Head Shape and Hair Type
hero_alt: Clippers taking the back of the head down short near the neckline
card_text: Where each one starts, what it does to the shape of your head, and how hair type and work settle the choice.
lede: A high fade starts up near the top of the side, where the head turns toward the crown, so most of the side is short and the top stands out. A low fade starts just above the ear and the neckline, so most of the side keeps its hair. Pick a high fade for contrast and a taller, narrower shape; pick a low fade for a softer look that hides more of the head's shape.
Here's how head shape, hair type and your week decide between them.

seo.title: High Fade vs Low Fade: How to Pick | Carlsbad, NM
seo.description: High fade vs low fade from a Carlsbad, NM barber: where each starts, how it changes your head shape, and which suits your hair type and job.

blocks.heading: Where the short part ends.
paragraphs: Both fades go from short at the bottom to longer at the top. The only real difference is how far up the short section climbs. On a high fade, it reaches close to the parietal ridge, the widest part of the head before it curves into the top. On a low fade, it stays in a narrow band around the ear and the nape.
The cut at the top of this post is a high fade under a short, even crop. Notice how little hair is left on the sides, and how that makes the front line-up and the top read sharper.
Between them sits the mid fade, which starts around the temple. If neither extreme sounds right, that's the usual answer.

The bottom of either one can finish at bare skin or keep a bit of shadow. That choice is separate from the height, so you can mix them: a high fade that stops at a shadow, or a low one taken all the way to skin.

blocks.heading: What each does to your outline.

subsections.heading: High fade
paragraphs: Taking the sides down high makes the head look narrower and the top look taller. That helps on a round face or a wide head. It also shows the true shape of your skull, so bumps, dips and scars along the side and back are on display.

subsections.heading: Low fade
paragraphs: Keeping hair on most of the side leaves more width and covers more of the head. That's kinder to an uneven back of the head and keeps a long or narrow face from looking even longer.

blocks.heading: Your hair has a say.
blocks.lead: Texture and color change the contrast.

subsections.heading: Dark, dense hair
paragraphs: Contrast is strongest here. A high fade on thick dark hair looks dramatic, and it also shows regrowth sooner. A low fade gives the same hair a calmer look.

subsections.heading: Curly and coily hair
paragraphs: Curls on top often look their sharpest over a high fade, because the tight sides frame the volume. A low fade works too when you'd rather the curls blend down the sides.

subsections.heading: Fine or thinning hair
paragraphs: A low fade keeps more weight around the head, which helps fine hair look fuller. A high fade on thin hair can leave the top looking sparse by comparison.

blocks.heading: Work, school, weekends.
paragraphs: A low fade is the safer choice for conservative workplaces and dress codes. It looks neat without making a statement, and it grows out quietly.
A high fade is the bolder look. Plenty of people wear one to work, but it draws more attention, and the short sides change faster as they grow.
If you want to try going higher, step up gradually. Start low or mid, then move it up next time. Raising a fade is quick. Lowering one means waiting for hair.
Hats and helmets count too. If you wear one most of the day, a low fade keeps the hair that peeks out under the brim looking even, while a high fade shows a hard line where the hat sits.

items.q: Is a high fade or low fade more professional?
items.a: A low fade usually reads more conservative. It keeps hair on the sides and softens as it grows.

items.q: Does a high fade suit a round face?
items.a: Often, yes. Short sides slim the head and make the top look taller.

items.q: Can a fade be high and still keep some hair at the bottom?
items.a: Yes. Height and how short the bottom goes are separate choices. A high fade can stop at a shadow instead of skin.

items.q: What about a low taper instead?
items.a: A low taper only shortens the edges, so it's even quieter than a low fade.
